title-group.article-title: Invented experiments on an erythroid enhancer at rs1427407

abstract.p: We describe invented experiments on an erythroid enhancer variant (rs1427407, chr2:60,490,908 T>G) for software tests.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Previous electrophoretic mobility shift assays in K562 nuclear extract showed that the T allele binds GATA1 more strongly than the G allele (Doe et al., 2010).

sec.title: Factor knockdown
sec.p: siRNA knockdown of GATA1 in K562 cells reduced BCL11A mRNA by half, and GATA1 occupancy at the enhancer fell.
Overexpression of GATA1 did not increase BCL11A mRNA in K562 cells.
siRNA knockdown of GATA1 did not change SORT1 mRNA in HepG2 cells.
siRNA knockdown of GATA1 in K562 cells lowered in vivo GATA1 occupancy at the enhancer and BCL11A mRNA.
Overexpression of GATA1 raised BCL11A mRNA twofold in K562 cells.

sec.title: Probe comparisons
sec.p: TAL1 binding was similar for both probes, whereas GATA-1 binding was threefold higher for the T allele probe.
The G allele probe bound GATA1 less strongly than the T allele probe, with a 103-fold difference in affinity (P = 3 × 10−8).
Affinity for GATA1 differed by 10³-fold between the T and G probes (P = 3 × 10⁻⁸), as “expected” from the motif.
As previously reported, the T allele probe bound GATA1 more strongly than the G allele probe in K562 extract.

sec.title: Genome editing
sec.p: Cas9 genome editing that introduced small indels at the SNP in HUDEP-2 cells (TT at rs1427407) lowered BCL11A mRNA by 40%.
CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of the enhancer containing rs1427407 in HUDEP-2 cells (TT at rs1427407) reduced BCL11A mRNA by 60%.
A 300-bp deletion of the enhancer in primary T cells lowered IL2 mRNA.
Mice lacking the enhancer had 40% lower plasma LDL cholesterol than wild-type littermates.
Targeting the enhancer with Cas9 lowered BCL11A mRNA in HUDEP-2 cells.

sec.title: Occupancy
sec.p: ChIP-qPCR showed GATA1 occupancy at the enhancer in K562 cells.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Our EMSA results show that the T allele probe bound GATA1 more strongly than the G allele probe in K562 extract.
